title: NFL Week 1 ties scoring record with 49.44 ppg average
dek: NFL teams combined for 791 points in Week 1 2026, averaging 49.44 points per game across all 16 games. This ties the post-merger high set in 2012. The Bears-Panthers game alone produced 96 points, a Week 1 record.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Week 1 2026 averaged 49.44 points per game, tying the post-merger high from 2012.
bottom_line: Whether Week 1's 49.44 ppg average persists through September will answer whether 2026 marks a sustained shift toward high-scoring games or a statistical outlier. The next two weeks of scoring totals will clarify whether the league has changed or whether specific week-one matchups created this spike.
body:
NFL teams combined for 791 points across Week 1 2026, averaging 49.44 points per game, according to Yahoo NFL. This ties the post-merger high set in 2012, making Week 1 2026 one of only two opening weeks since the merger to reach this scoring level.
The Bears-Panthers game alone produced a Week 1 record 96 points, per Yahoo. The Lions defeated the Saints in overtime after New Orleans missed a two-point conversion on the final play, per CBS Sports. Detroit had led 21-0 with five minutes remaining in the third quarter. In other high-scoring Week 1 contests, the Bills defeated the Texans 36-31, the Cardinals beat the Chargers 26-14, and the Bengals defeated the Buccaneers 33-27, per CBS Sports.
Quarterback performances reflected the offensive outburst. Lamar Jackson went 17-for-25 for 324 yards with 13 yards per attempt, threw one touchdown and ran for another in Week 1, per CBS Sports. On under-center, play-action plays, Jackson was 5-for-5 for 101 yards. Baker Mayfield, however, struggled for Tampa Bay, losing three fumbles and taking four sacks in the Buccaneers' loss to Cincinnati.
Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers was officially active despite a knee injury for Week 1, per CBS Sports.
Two notable quarterbacks returned from injury.  He did not play in the preseason. Bo Nix fractured his ankle in January, per CBS Sports.
CBS Sports analysis suggested caution about extrapolating Week 1's scoring to the broader season. The Texans' defense was described as having an aggressive style that got beat by big plays downfield by Josh Allen, with the framing that such performances are cyclical, not systemic. Baker Mayfield's three-fumble performance was contextualized as a single-week anomaly, with one analysis stating: "There are some high highs and some low lows. Week 1 can be all over the place."
